title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem: Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Anika Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical reference for Redwood private deployments: VPC-hosted and on-premises installations. It consolidates reference architectures, packaging requirements, a customer prerequisites library, day-2 operational runbooks, and rigorous upgrade & rollback procedures. The goal is a repeatable, auditable path for onboarding enterprise customers with predictable SLAs and minimal operational risk.

Scope

- Target audience: SREs, Solutions Engineers, Customer Ops, and on‑prem integrators.
- Includes: network & security layout, hardware and software packaging, pre-deployment customer checklist, runbooks for monitoring/alerts/backups, and step‑by‑step upgrade/rollback playbook.
- Excludes: onboarding commercial integrations (handled in sales enablement) and model-specific tuning (see model-onboarding).

Reference Architectures (high level)

1) VPC Deployment (recommended for cloud-hosted customer-controlled deployments)

- Components: Private control plane (customer-managed), Redwood runtime cluster (Kubernetes), optional GPU node pools, NAT/egress gateway, internal load balancers, KMS/HSM integration, metrics & logging endpoints.
- Network topology: minimum three subnets across two AZs: control-plane, runtime (compute), and storage. Use private route tables and enforced security groups.
- Data plane considerations: prefer TLS-in-transit + mTLS between services. KV cache and model artifacts stored in customer S3-compatible storage with IAM roles for access.

2) On‑Prem Deployment (recommended for air‑gapped or regulated customers)

- Components: OVA or container bundle, orchestration (RKE2/AKS-on-prem/OpenShift tested), local object store (MinIO) optional, hardware GPU drivers and CUDA/cuDNN pinned to validated versions, on‑prem KMS connector or HSM integration.
- Connectivity: if air-gapped, provide offline package and signed manifests; for hybrid, use outbound-only control-plane egress over TLS with IP allowlists.

Packaging & Installation

- Packaging formats we support: Helm charts (preferred for cloud VPC), OCI images, and tarball-based appliances for fully offline installs. Packages include: runtime container images, model artifact manifests, packaging metadata, and a signed checksum bundle.
- Supported OS & host requirements (minimum):

  | Component | Minimum | Recommended |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Host OS | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS |
  | Kernel | 5.4+ | 5.15+ |
  | Docker/CRI | containerd 1.5+ | containerd 1.6+ |
  | Kubernetes | 1.21+ | 1.24+ |
  | GPU Drivers | NVIDIA 470+ | NVIDIA 520+ |

- Container images are signed with our internal GPG keys; on-prem installs must verify signatures. Offline install flow: transfer package -> verify signature -> install base dependencies -> apply manifests -> validate health checks.

Customer Requirements Library (pre-deployment checklist)

Provide this checklist to the customer prior to engagement. Must be validated by SE and solutions architect.

1) Identity & Access
- Primary contact and emergency oncall (name, email, pager).
- Service account with least privilege for object storage access (S3 role or MinIO user).
- KMS/HSM access method and credentials or connector details.

2) Network & Security
- VPC/subnet CIDRs and preferred AZs.
- Egress/Ingress policies, NAT gateway details, IP allowlist for Redwood support endpoints.
- TLS certificates (CA or public) or plan to use Let's Encrypt (cloud).

3) Compute & Storage
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency (tokens/sec) to size GPU pools.
- Node sizing recommendation table (example):
  - Small: 1x A10/GPU equivalent per 100 concurrent requests (batching dependent).
  - Medium: 4x A40 per node pool for higher throughput.
  - Storage: 1TB NVMe per model shard minimum; object store with 99.9% durability.

4) Compliance & Data Residency
- Classification of data sent to Redwood runtime (PII, regulated).
- Retention windows for logs and metrics; any requirements for syslog forwarding.

5) Operational Access & Monitoring
- Metrics endpoint (Prometheus) accessibility, TLS certs, and scraping credentials.
- Log forwarder (Fluentd/Fluent Bit) destination and credentials.

Day‑2 Operations (runbook excerpt)

Monitoring & Alerting
- Baseline dashboards (Console): per-route latency, per-model token/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and queue sizes.
- Recommended SLOs: 95th percentile tail latency <= 300ms for small generation calls; error rate < 0.5% per hour.
- Key alerts: node OOM, pod restart rate > 5/hr, GPU temperature > 85°C, persistent queue depth > configured thresholds.

Routine Maintenance
1) Daily checks
- Verify cluster health: kubectl get nodes, kubectl get pods -A | grep CrashLoopBackOff.
- Verify model cache hit rate > expected baseline.
2) Weekly
- Rotate ephemeral keys per customer policy.
- Review storage consumption and clean temporary model shards >30 days old.
3) Monthly
- Apply non-breaking security patches and run e2e smoke tests.

Backups & Disaster Recovery
- Back up metadata (model manifests, routing policies, rollout states) daily to customer S3.
- Snapshot schedules for persistent volumes (weekly full, daily incremental).
- Recovery time objective (RTO): 2 hours for control-plane failover, 4-8 hours for full model rehydration depending on model size and network.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures

Prerequisites
- Confirm backup of control-plane metadata and model manifests.
- Have rollback image tags and previous Helm chart available.
- Confirm maintenance window and customer acknowledgement.

Canary Upgrade (recommended)
1) Stage: deploy new runtime image to a small canary node pool (5-10% of capacity).
2) Smoke tests: run the full e2e test suite (latency, accuracy checks for representative prompts, and load tests at 10% traffic).
3) Monitoring window: observe for 30-60 minutes for any regressions (error rates, latency tails, GPU errors).
4) Gradual rollout: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% by scaling node pool weights and adjusting routing policies.

Rollback (if failure detected)
1) Immediately shift traffic away from failing pool to last known-good pool.
2) Apply previous Helm chart with --reuse-values and previous image tag.
3) Validate health checks and run smoke tests.
4) Postmortem: open an incident review and tag the release.

Emergency rollback (fast path)
- If canary shows critical failure (service unavailable or severe correctness regression), scale canary to zero and re-route traffic, then promote previous stable pool. Notify customer and oncall.

Upgrade validation matrix (sample checks)
- Functional: API health, inference correctness on golden prompts.
- Performance: P95 latency within 10% of baseline, throughput within 5%.
- Resource: GPU memory footprint <= baseline + 10%.

Operational Playbook: Example Commands
- Verify cluster: kubectl get nodes -o wide
- Rollout helm: helm upgrade redwood-runtime ./chart -f values.yaml --timeout 15m
- Rollback helm: helm rollback redwood-runtime 3 --wait
- Verify model health: curl -sS https://localhost:8443/health/models | jq

Appendix: Example Helm values (abbreviated)

-- values.yaml --
runtime:
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime
    tag: 2026.04.1
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    requests:
      cpu: "2000m"
      memory: "8Gi"
network:
  prometheus:
    enabled: true
    tls: true
